To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the uptake and utilization of nucleosides in microplasmods of Physarum is unique in that the nucleoside moiety is readily metabolized while the purine base moiety is not taken up.
the uptake and incorporation of nucleosides is much more pronounced in microplasmdoia of P. polycephalum than that of the free purine bases.

purine nucleosidase phosphorylase (EC 2.4.2.1) is a very important enzyme in the purine metabolism of Physarum and that the deoxyribosyl moiety cannot be utilised as a source of deoxyribonuclearotides.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the uptake and incorporation of nucleosides into the nucleotide pools of Physarum microplasmodial cells.
the elucidation of the pathways of purine nucleotide biosynthesis and with the effects of various inhibitors on the growth of Physarum.
the elucidation of the metabolic pathways involved in the incorporation of purine bases and nucleosides into the nucleotide pool of the microplasmodium of Physarum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the microplasmodium of P. polycephalum is a purine auxotroph.
the uptake and incorporation of exogenous purine base analogs is negligible.
purine nucleosidase phosphorylase and purine nucleosidoses are not only present in Physarum but are also the only pathways for purine nucleosido incorporation into nucleotides.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
purine bases are not taken up by the microplasmodium and that the ribonucleoside and deoxyribonucloside phosphates are the only compounds that can enter the cells and be metabolised.
purine nucleosidase phosphorylase and purine phosphorribosyltransferase are important in purine metabolism of microplasmodium, while purine kinase is not.
the uptake and metabolism of purine nucleotides is not only a function of the cell wall but also a function of the membrane of the microplasmodium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the purine metabolism in Physarum microplasmodias is very similar to that in higher eucaryotes.
the uptake and utilization of nucleosides in Physarum is not a reflection of a general mechanism for purine nucleotide biosynthesis, as has been suggested for other organisms.

purine nucleosidase phosphorylase is the main enzyme responsible for the degradation of purine nucleo-sides in the slime mould Physarum polycepha-lum, and that the purine phospho-ribosyltransferases are not involved in the uptake or degradation of free purine bases.
